name: Espejo — site of Capa's 'Falling Soldier'
story: Robert Capa's photograph of a militiaman falling backwards, published in Vu on 23 September 1936 and in Life in 1937, became the defining image of the war. For decades it was said to show the anarchist Federico Borrell García killed at Cerro Muriano, north of Córdoba, on 5 September 1936. In 2009 José Manuel Susperregui matched the skyline to the outskirts of Espejo, about 50 km away, where the front was quiet at the time; many now think the picture was staged or taken during an exercise. Espejo shows how the Córdoba front lines ran through open countryside in the first summer.
see: The open, rolling farmland around Espejo, whose skyline was matched to the photographs; no memorial or marker is known.
plan: Drive around the outskirts of Espejo with a copy of the photograph; the fields are private farmland, so view from tracks.

boxes.text: view it from the road or public path only.
Location (Cerro Muriano vs Espejo), identity of the soldier and whether the scene was staged are all disputed.
